name: Shechem son of Hamor
summary: Shechem, prince of the country, saw Dinah, took her, and lay with her and defiled her. He then asked for her in marriage and agreed to circumcision to get her. Her brothers answered with the sword.
offense: He had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter, which thing ought not to be done. The law would later require the seducer of an unbetrothed virgin to endow her and the rapist to die.
judgment: On the third day, while the men of the city were sore, Simeon and Levi killed every male, Hamor and Shechem among them, and took Dinah out of his house. Jacob condemned the manner of it; the brothers answered, should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?

lawsResolved.text: A rapist is to be put to death.
If a man entices a woman not engaged, and lies with her, he must endow her to be his wife.
It is the will of God that you abstain from fornication and sexual immorality.

text.text: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.

And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.

And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.
And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went out.
And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?
If a man find a damsel that is a virgin, which is not betrothed, and lay hold on her, and lie with her, and they be found;
Then the man that lay with her shall give unto the damsel’s father fifty shekels of silver, and she shall be his wife; because he hath humbled her, he may not put her away all his days.
And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.
If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.
